pr_body:
Fixes #28792.

The interface for these has been experimental for years, and we know that the design is incomplete and needs work.
Having this around slows progress in other areas, and so it seems prudent to cull them and re-implement when we have a design we believe in.

Note that this does cause some tests for RBAC to be not implementable, so I suspect we'll want to think for five minutes on an appropriate solution for that.

pr_comments: The last I thought of taking this out, I remember the discussion being along the lines of - whenever we do reimplement this, the design would probably look the same as what we already have, so let's not annoy users who are looking forward to this feature by deleting what we already have.

I could probably buy that for the C++ API (although we haven't worked through the security bits as a team, so hard to say)
I think implementation wise we'd probably choose non-encoded metadata to carry the configuration, and potentially locate the get encoding elsewhere in the stack.
(I suspect a library used by transports to do the GET request encoding would end up being substantially cleaner)
Also, @dennycd should review the ObjC changes.

Thought: I can pretty trivially write a unit test on the get behavior when I convert this filter to promises, and that conversion is trivial to do once this change goes in.

So, @markdroth how about an iou with a promise of one business day between submission of this PR and the appearance of a new one with an appropriate test and converted to promises?

Craig, if the tests I suggested above won't work for some reason, then I like your suggestion of doing this as a unit test for the individual filter.  But I'd like to understand (from @yashykt) why the suggestion above wouldn't work first.

issue_context.title: Remove (experimental) PUT support
issue_context.body:
At least one user used PUT without realizing it is an incomplete experiment, much more so than other experimental APIs. https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/2881#issuecomment-1030038253 (and b/217892555). That caused compatibility issues when Go improved its implementation to verify the HTTP method is POST.

I believe I heard @yashykt recently removed the GET support in C (but I failed to find the PR quickly; "get" is hard to search for). Yes, PUT probably has very low maintenance burden, but grpc dev interest in PUT is lower than that of GET, so at this point it seems best to remove the API. If we don't want to do that, I guess we can put a "DO NOT USE" message in the docs.

CC @markdroth, @bdhess, @dfawley
comments: The last I looked at it, we decided not to remove GET/PUT support, but @ctiller just put out https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/28922
@yashykt, if GET is still present, how was the HTTP method handled for RBAC?

> @yashykt, if GET is still present, how was the HTTP method handled for RBAC?

It was handled similar to other metadata types. (The method metadata was already available to the rbac filter implementation)

review_comments:
Ideally on iOS, we split this into two steps ( deprecation -> removal), instead of doing a hard build break.  But looks like this API is a "semi-public" (private to bazel/blaze codegen users, but public for anyone directly using GRPCCallSafety).  Can we at least mark this as deprecated instead of removal ?   

```objc 

  GRPCCallSafetyIdempotentRequest __attribute__((deprecated("GRPCCallSafetyIdempotentRequest is deprecated."))) = 1,

  GRPCCallSafetyCacheableRequest __attribute__((deprecated("GRPCCallSafetyCacheableRequest is deprecated."))) = 2,
```

g3 internal seems ok (cs shows no existing usage), but OSS side this at least given the devs a chance to fix their code when picking up the change. Thanks !
Is the proposal here to leave the enums in (marked deprecated) but silently change the behavior?
Denny reached out offline, and my summary seems to be he'd be fine with simply removing these... is that right @dennycd

Thanks Craig ! yes chatted offline yesterday and looked into this a bit further. Since this is not a published API that we officially support, breaking change is better than an implicit behavior change (even with deprecation warning, some iOS projects may not turn on treat-deprecation-as-error flag) . Please go ahead w/ the removal ; )
I think we also no longer need the `read_stream` or `have_read_stream` data members.
fixed
@yashykt, does this test still have any value without the ability to test other methods?
Hmm, I guess we'll need testing (or some way to be confident) that all other method types are rejected. Otherwise, this test is not really needed.

I want to make sure that we don't open ourselves to a security-related bug here.  [gRFC A41](https://github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A41-xds-rbac.md) says:
> For this design, `headers` can include `:method`, `:authority`, and `:path` matchers and they should match the values received on-the-wire independent of whether they are stored in Metadata or in separate APIs. `:method` can be hard-coded to `POST` if unavailable and a code audit confirms the server denies requests for all other method types.

Do we have a guarantee that the transport will reject GET or PUT requests once this PR goes in?  If so, then that offers at least some assurance that the current behavior will be correct, even without the tests.  But it's really not the same as having a test.

Perhaps more importantly, if we re-add support for GET or PUT in the future, how will we remember to re-add these tests?

CC @ejona86 for his input as well.
[http_server_filter.cc does this](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/28922/files#diff-ecfb39bf6f4efc0bacabfded858c2346ef3b07c91babb8cbc5d4f286b28b70deL125)

Okay.  But I think we should at least keep the test that shows that the rules does match when it specifies that the method is POST, since we know that we're going to hit that case.

For the negative case, how about having a rule that checks that the method is GET and showing that it does not match?
Given that we will be removing the infrastructure to send requests with GET/PUT, this would mean we would need to handcraft those requests.

I'm not proposing that we craft a different request -- all requests will continue to be POST.  I'm suggesting that we have one test with a rule that requires the method to be POST that does match, and another test with a rule that requires the method to be GET that does *not* match.
Done
@yashykt Same question here.
Same here. I guess we'll need testing (or some way to be confident) that all other method types are rejected. Otherwise, this test is not really needed.
Same as above: I think we still need tests here for both the positive and negative match cases.

Do we plan to introduce new request features in the near term ? if not, this removal basically renders the entire GRPCCallSafety enum obsolete. I can create a follow up TODO to remove the enum if that's the case. Thanks

I think that would be reasonable to do!

I'm not aware of any upcoming features that would want a similar API, @markdroth?
No immediate plans, no.  But in the long run, I would not be surprised if we wind up re-adding GET support.
Looks like you accidentally removed this one here.  I think it needs to stay.
